MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 2, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:02 p.m., on June 2, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 28, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: 1 potential case.

CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

City Council Minutes  1  June 2, 2014
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Reardon

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two matters in Closed Session.
The City Council gave direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim the Month of June "RELAY FOR LIFE and Paint our Town Purple
  Month"

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to members of the Relay for Life Committee.

P2.  Recognize the Castille Elementary School 4th and 5th Grade Math Team on their
  Outstanding Achievements and Placing First in the Rubik Cube Challenge at the
  Orange County Math Field Day

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of appreciation to Coach Lisa Klaes, Teacher and
  Coach Shonna Josephson, and members of the Castille 4th and 5th Grade Math Team
  who gave a Rubik Cube demonstration.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Norm Bour representing Vapors.com: noted that his client has an e-cigarette kiosk inside the
Mission Viejo Mall and the City has asked them to provide a Conditional Use Permit. He
requested that the decision be rescinded because they do not believe that the kiosk falls under the
category of a retail store or a vapor lounge.

Robert D. Breton, M.V.: expressed his support for agenda item 7 and stated that having an
orchestra of this quality at no cost to the attendees is invaluable. Mr. Breton stated that the
Cultural Arts Committee will continue to help fund the Pacific Symphony event in future years.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: reminded the Council that he advised them of the Orange County
Fire Authority’s $665 million unfunded liabilities at a previous meeting and that due to this
problem, the financial reserves of the City are under intense threat.

City Council Minutes  2  June 2, 2014
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 7, and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 19, 2014, as presented.

5.  Selection of Independent Auditor for the Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2014 and June
  30, 2015

  Awarded a contract to Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP (RAMS) to serve as the
  City's Independent Auditors for the Fiscal Years ending June 30, 2014, and June 30, 2015.

6.  General Municipal Election - November 4, 2014

  (1) Adopted Resolution 14-18 Calling for the Holding of a General Municipal Election to
  be Held on Tuesday, November 4, 2014, for the Election of Certain Officers as Required by
  the Provisions of the Laws of the State of California Relating to General Law; (2) adopted
  Resolution 14-19 Requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Orange to
  Consolidate a General Municipal Election to be Held on November 4, 2014 with the
  Statewide General Election to be Held on the Same Date pursuant to Â§ 10403 of the
  Elections Code; (3) adopted Resolution 14-20 Adopting Regulations for Candidates for
  Elective Officer Pertaining to Candidates Statements Submitted to the Voters at an Election
  to be Held on November 4, 2014; and (4) directed the City Clerk to schedule the adoption
  of the resolution citing the election results and administration of the oath to the newly
  elected Council Members on December 1, 2014, or as soon as possible thereafter.

8.  Agreement with the County of Orange for the Point of Dispensing (POD) Exercise

  Approved the agreement for provision of point of dispensing site services between the
City Council Minutes  3  June 2, 2014
   County of Orange and the City of Mission Viejo from July 1, 2014, through June 30, 2015.

9.  Los Alisos Boulevard Pavement Rehabilitation: Interstate 5 to Santa Margarita
  Parkway (CIP 837)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt in
  the amount of $2,111,111; and (2) authorized the City Manager to enter into a cost-share
  agreement with the City of Lake Forest.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

7.  Partnership Agreement with Pacific Symphony Orchestra for the Symphony in the
  Cities Summer Concert

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the 2014 Pacific Symphony concert: Sue Crowson,
  M.V.; Lillian Arand, M.V. and Pam Blaine, representing Pacific Symphony Orchestra,
  M.V.

  The following presented a written comment in support of the Pacific Symphony concerts in
  the park: Helen Workun, M.V.

  Council Member Schlicht noted that she is not against the concert but she is against
  government funding regional events with taxpayer dollars. She stated that the Pacific
  Symphony should seek a new corporate sponsor instead of asking the City to fund the
  concert.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) adopt Resolution
  14-21 Amending the FY 13-14 Cultural Arts Budget in the General Fund; and (2) authorize
  the City Manager to sign the Symphony in the Cities 2014 Partnership Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

11. FY 2014-15 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.
City Council Minutes  4  June 2, 2014
   Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: announced that three years ago he requested that staff
  investigate police cost savings that have been implemented by other cities and by the
  County and as far as he knows, nothing has been done. Mr. Wontrobski asked the Council
  to wait two weeks on approval of this Sheriff’s Department contract until the City of
  Laguna Hills’ police cost saving study is published on June 10.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1) approve the
  FY 2014-15 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange (A14-16)
  for an amount not to exceed $17,086,147; (2) authorize staff to issue a purchase order in an
  amount not to exceed $16,100,000 to the County of Orange for Law Enforcement Services
  for FY 2014-15; and (3) authorize the City Manager to approve reimbursements related to
  special enforcement services in an amount not to exceed $65,000 for FY 2014-15.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: addressing item #5 (which was approved as part of the Consent
Calendar) he asked, if it is determined that the City is ultimately liable for its share of the OCFA
JPA unfunded liability, must the City report such information on the City’s financial statements?

3.  Check Register dated May 9, 2014 in the amount of $195,623.32

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about payments to Ebsco Subscription Services, Green
  Angels Security and Tomark Sports, Inc.

  Staff provided answers to the questions or agreed to respond with information after
  researching the payments.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  June 2, 2014
 4.  Check Register dated May 16, 2014 in the amount of $2,289,118.54

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about payments to Aileen May and Joy Aldridge for the
  Bears about Town projects and asked for an update on the project. She also asked about a
  payment to Blais and Associates and she wondered if they are trolling for dollars.

  Mr. Wilberg responded that Blais seeks grant opportunities for a variety of issues and
  projects and the City, in turn, asks Blais to find funding for specific projects as they come
  up. He noted that the City is only charged for time spent not a flat rate or percentage.

  Council Member Schlicht also inquired about payments to Martin Laser for dog park
  pavers, Connie Phillips for a goal setting workshop and RJM Design Group.

  Staff provided responses and/or agreed to get back to the Council with further information.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10. Claim Against the City - Julie Bronson

  City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht noted that she is uncomfortable with the City's insurance and
  indemnification at the Nadadores facility and she would like to follow this case from
  beginning to end to see how it is being handled.

  City Attorney Curley responded that staff will keep the Council apprised of the matter as it
  unfolds.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to reject the
  claim.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  June 2, 2014
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: announced that he attended an equitable adjustment hearing
  regarding a lawsuit that the City of Irvine has filed against the OCFA. He stated that the
  Judge directed the parties to submit additional briefs and he expressed concern with the
  City's JPA agreement with OCFA related to the Equity Issue.

  Council Member Leckness presented the report on the OCFA meeting that he attended on
  behalf of Mayor Kelley.

  Mayor Kelley provided updates on some of the issues that are taking place at OCFA.

13. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury announced that he was unable to attend the last meeting of the
  OCTA.

14. Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2014 League of California Cities Annual
  Conference

  By consensus, the City Council appointed Mayor Kelley as voting delegate and Council
  Member Reardon as alternate for the League of California Cities Conference Annual
  Business Meeting on September 5, 2014.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

RECESS

At the hour of 8:32 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:45
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Attorney’s Report

15. Ordinance to Repeal City Ordinance No. 12-292 and Thereby Remove Chapter 11.23
  of Title 11 from the Mission Viejo Municipal Code

  City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  introduce Ordinance No. 14-303 Repealing Ordinance No. 12-292 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code.

City Council Minutes  7  June 2, 2014
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she voted no in protest and to stand up for the
  Constitutional rights of children.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon discussed her attendance at the Girl Scouts Silver and Gold Awards
Ceremony where she was the keynote speaker. She mentioned that the Gold Award is often
compared to the Boy Scouts Eagle Award however it is somewhat different in that the girls have
to come up with their own project and there is a lot of scrutiny in the process. At the ceremony,
35 girls received the Silver Award and 11 girls received the Gold Award. Council Member
Reardon read descriptions of some of the girls' topics for their projects and she expressed her
amazement that so many young people are doing such marvelous things in the community and
she said we have a lot to be proud about and grateful for. She also expressed appreciation for the
troop leaders and parents who are investing their lives in these kids and she stated that it is
simply amazing.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she feels bad about the situation with the child safety
zones in city parks. She said that it is funny that sex predators want forgiveness and redemption
but they have scarred a life forever. She stated that she can't put her mind around the fact that
these predators have lost many of their rights after their felony conviction yet they demand
access to parks where children play and the courts have allowed them that access. Council
Member Schlicht expressed her concerns with the Pacific Symphony concert and stated that it is
a great community event but we can't have everyone coming to government all the time to fund
events. She noted that the Pacific Symphony lost corporate funding and they should go replace
that instead of coming to the City to pick up their pay. She also expressed that she doesn’t think
it's appropriate to spend over $5,000 for a private VIP party after the concert and she feels that it
is morally wrong. Council Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at recent events including
the screening of a movie called Blue Beats Green which had some very valid arguments against
climate change. She stated that money is behind the theory of climate change and she read a
statement on the matter from Dr. Spencer, a NASA scientist. She feels that the media and
City Council Minutes  8  June 2, 2014
 government are behind the hype and taxpayers end up paying extra money because of something
that is naturally occurring. Council Member Schlicht also discussed her attendance at the new
Farmers Market at Mission Hills Church and the American Legion pancake breakfast which
supports Boy Scout Troop 862. She noted that the Memorial Day service honored our country’s
warriors and it was a very solemn ceremony. She reminded residents to go out and vote
tomorrow and she observed that she is proud that Mission Viejo has a higher voter turnout than
most communities. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from
Congressional candidate Greg Raths: "Do you know who in Congress will look after our
veterans? Veterans.”

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury stated that the City put on a wonderful Memorial Day ceremony. It seems
to get bigger and bigger every year, not only with the people that are honored but the number of
people that show up. Council Member Ury noted that it is one of their duties as leaders in the
City to honor those who have sacrificed for the Country. He thanked staff and stated that he is
looking forward to next year’s Memorial Day observance.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness discussed his visit to the home of a resident who is bothered by his
neighbor's overgrown trees and wants to have them cut down. He went out to see the situation
and unfortunately, Mayor Pro Tem Leckness had to tell the resident that he cannot touch the
trees. The homeowners Mr. Leckness visited have a beautiful yard and their home will be on the
City's upcoming garden tour. He further outlined his attendance at the grand opening of the
Infiniti dealership and he discussed a resident’s new karate studio venture and wished him
luck. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness agreed with Mayor Kelley that staff was very resourceful when
it came to this year’s Pacific Symphony Orchestra concert. He stated that it is so much easier to
not put on a program like this yet the City Manager and Assistant City Manager figured out how
to find the money and he stated that it’s absolutely important to the community to have a
connection to the arts. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Leckness wished Council Member Ury success in
tomorrow’s election and he stated that the City’s loss will be the County’s gain.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley introduced the City’s new OCFA Battalion Chief, Chief Henry. She commended
staff on another wonderful Memorial Day ceremony and she noted that the event has grown in
size and quality. She thanked Colonel Joe Russell from the City’s adopted Marines for giving an
excellent speech as well as veteran Tom Spry who is a very rare soldier for having served in
several wars. She also thanked Bagels and Brew for providing refreshments. Mayor Kelley
outlined her attendance at recent events including the Orange County Triathlon which drew a
large number of athletes from our own community and from all over the nation, and an Eagle
Court of honor ceremony for two really impressive young men. She reminded residents that the
Relay for Life will be held this weekend beginning Saturday, June 7 at 9:00 a.m. and ending on
Sunday, June 8 at 9:00 a.m. Mayor Kelley thanked her colleagues for wearing purple this
evening to promote the event and she encouraged residents to go out and show their support this
City Council Minutes  9  June 2, 2014
 weekend. She announced that the Community of Character quality for the month of June is
citizenship and the character movie, Citizen Kane, will be shown on Sunday June 22 in the
Council Chamber. The event is free with a discussion of the character quality following the
movie. In closing, Mayor Kelley asked the community for prayers for the Sheer family who lost
4 lives and the little girl who drowned this past weekend.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:15 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of the Sheer family and the family of a young
drowning victim, to Monday, June 16, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting June 16, 2014

City Council Minutes  10  June 2, 2014
